title: The Stolen King: How Rajaraja Chola Came Home
style: Photorealistic historical documentary footage, shot on ARRI Alexa with anamorphic lenses, natural skin texture, real fabric movement, natural light, film grain, shallow depth of field. No text, no subtitles, no captions, no watermark.
negative_prompt: cartoon, animation, 3d render, CGI look, plastic skin, extra fingers, deformed hands, distorted face, text, subtitles, watermark, logo, modern clothing in ancient scenes, gopuram gateway tower as main tower

characters.KING: a regal Tamil king in his fifties with deep brown skin, a neatly trimmed grey-streaked moustache and long dark hair tied in a top knot, bare-chested, wearing layered gold necklaces, gold armlets and earrings, and a white silk veshti with a wide gold border
characters.YOUNG_KING: a regal Tamil prince of about thirty-five with deep brown skin, a black moustache and long black hair tied in a top knot, bare-chested, wearing gold necklaces and armlets and a white silk veshti with a gold border
characters.TEMPLE: the Brihadisvara temple of Thanjavur: a single enormous pyramidal granite tower built directly over the sanctum, rising in thirteen tapering tiers of carved miniature shrines and crowned by one rounded octagonal stone dome with a small gold finial, standing in a vast stone-paved courtyard surrounded by a long pillared cloister
characters.BRONZE_KING: a 75-centimetre-tall antique Chola bronze statue of a standing king with his hands joined in prayer, wearing a tall crown, with a dark green-brown patina
characters.BRONZE_QUEEN: a slightly smaller antique Chola bronze statue of a standing queen in graceful tribhanga pose with a tall crown, dark green-brown patina

shots.prompt: Night, 1960s, inside a dim stone temple hall with massive carved granite pillars. A single kerosene lantern on the floor. Two men seen only from behind and in silhouette, faces hidden in shadow, carefully lift a small bronze statue off a stone pedestal and wrap it in old white cloth. Slow handheld push-in, tense, quiet. Sound: crickets, distant dog bark, cloth rustling.
shots.narration: Sometime in the 1960s, inside the greatest temple in South India, two small bronze statues quietly disappeared. No alarm. No police report. For almost fifty years, hardly anyone noticed.

shots.prompt: Close-up of an empty carved stone pedestal in a dark temple niche, a faint clean outline in the dust where a statue once stood, a small brass oil lamp flickering beside it. Very slow push-in. Sound: lamp flame, quiet temple echo.
shots.narration: One of them may be the only portrait of a great Tamil emperor made while he was still alive. The emperor who built this temple. Rajaraja Chola.

shots.prompt: Slow cinematic drone push-in toward the great temple tower, soft morning light moving across the carved stone, clouds drifting, a few birds circling the top. Keep the architecture exactly as in the image. Sound: wind, birds, a single deep temple bell.
shots.narration: This is the story of how a thousand-year-old king was stolen. And how, against all odds, he finally came home.

shots.prompt: The year 985, a royal court in South India lit by hundreds of oil lamps, carved wooden pillars and silk canopies. {YOUNG_KING} sits on a carved throne as an elderly priest places a gold crown on his head. Courtiers in white veshtis bow. Slow dolly in on the king's face, calm and determined. Sound: conch shells, drums, chanting.
shots.narration: In the year 985, a prince named Arulmozhi Varman was crowned king of the Cholas. He took a new name. Rajaraja. King of kings.

shots.prompt: A Chola war fleet of large wooden sailing ships with square cloth sails and tiger banners crossing a stormy blue ocean at sunrise, soldiers with spears and shields on deck, waves crashing over the bows. Aerial tracking shot. Sound: waves, wind in sails, drums.
shots.narration: Over the next thirty years, he turned a southern kingdom into an empire. His armies crossed into Sri Lanka. His ships sailed as far as the Maldives.

shots.prompt: Close-up of skilled stone engravers carving old Tamil script into a granite temple wall by oil-lamp light, chisels and mallets, stone dust floating in a beam of light, focused faces of the craftsmen. Sound: rhythmic tapping of chisels.
shots.narration: And unlike most rulers of his age, he made sure everything was written down. In stone.

shots.prompt: Around the year 1005, a vast construction site in South India: hundreds of workers and elephants haul huge granite blocks on wooden rollers up a long earthen ramp toward a half-built pyramidal granite temple tower wrapped in wooden scaffolding. Dust, heat haze, golden afternoon light. Wide crane shot. Sound: crowd shouting, elephants trumpeting, ropes creaking.
shots.narration: Around the year 1003, he began his greatest project. A temple to Shiva in his capital, Thanjavur.

shots.prompt: Close-up of a sculptor's weathered hands carving a granite figure of a dancer with an iron chisel, sparks and stone chips flying, sweat on his arms, then rack focus to dozens of other carvers working in rows under palm-leaf shades. Sound: chisels on stone, distant chanting.
shots.narration: There is no granite near Thanjavur. Every block was brought from far away. And granite is one of the hardest stones on earth. These carvers shaped it with iron tools, and patience.

shots.prompt: Very slow low-angle tilt up the full height of the temple tower toward the dome at the top, clouds moving behind it, sunlight sliding across the carved tiers. Keep the architecture exactly as in the image. Sound: wind, distant bells.
shots.narration: The tower above the shrine rises about sixty-six metres. Thirteen tapering tiers of stone. One of the tallest temple towers in the world at the time.

shots.prompt: Around the year 1009, dozens of workers on top of a nearly finished pyramidal granite temple tower guide an enormous rounded octagonal stone dome into place with thick ropes and wooden levers, the city and green fields far below, dramatic sky. Aerial orbit shot. Sound: wind, men shouting commands, ropes straining.
shots.narration: At the very top sits a massive domed stone. Exactly how it was lifted so high, a thousand years ago, is still debated today.
In 1010, the temple was finished. The king named it Rajarajeswaram.

shots.prompt: Evening in the year 1011 in the stone courtyard of {TEMPLE}: temple dancers in silk perform beside musicians playing nadaswaram and drums, lamp lighters fill rows of brass lamps, priests carry flowers, crowds of townspeople in simple cotton clothes watch. Warm lamp light, slow gliding camera through the crowd. Sound: nadaswaram music, drums, crowd murmur.
shots.narration: An inscription on its walls names more than six hundred people who served here. Dancers, musicians, lamp lighters, tailors, accountants. This was not just a temple. It was a city inside a city.

shots.prompt: Night in an ancient bronze-casting workshop: craftsmen pour glowing molten bronze from a clay crucible into a clay mould buried in sand, orange light on their faces and bare arms, smoke and sparks. Slow push-in. Sound: roaring fire, bubbling metal, bellows.
shots.narration: In the twenty-ninth year of Rajaraja's reign, a chieftain from Kodumbalur gave the temple thirteen bronze images.

shots.prompt: Inside a dim stone shrine lit only by small brass oil lamps, two antique bronze sculptures stand side by side on a carved stone pedestal: a standing man with a tall crown and his palms pressed together, and a slightly smaller standing woman with a tall crown in a graceful pose. Dark green-brown patina, strings of white jasmine flowers. Slow arc around the two sculptures, lamp flames reflecting on the metal. Sound: soft chanting, lamp flames.
shots.narration: Two of them were special. A bronze of Rajaraja himself, hands joined in prayer. And beside him, his queen, Lokamadevi. Each about seventy-five centimetres tall.

shots.prompt: Extreme close-up, very slow push-in on the serene face of {BRONZE_KING}, lamp light flickering across the patinated bronze, dust particles floating, shallow depth of field. Sound: a single soft bell, silence.
shots.narration: Historians believe these were made while the king was still alive. If that is true, this may be the closest we will ever get to seeing his face.

shots.prompt: 1960s colour film look, faded and grainy: an old temple caretaker in a white veshti walks slowly with an oil lamp through a long dark stone hall with carved pillars, passing statues in niches. Slight handheld. Sound: footsteps, crickets.
shots.narration: For more than nine hundred years, they stayed in the temple. Then, sometime in the 1960s, they were gone.

shots.prompt: 1960s, night: a small bronze statue wrapped in cloth is placed into a wooden crate in the back of an old truck, a man's hands nail the lid shut under a weak streetlight, then the truck drives away down an empty dusty road. Grainy film look. Sound: hammering, old engine starting, crickets.
shots.narration: Police would later say the originals had been swapped for copies. The real bronzes left Tamil Nadu.

shots.prompt: A quiet, dim private museum gallery with dark wood and soft spotlights: {BRONZE_KING} displayed alone inside a glass case on a wooden plinth, nobody around. Slow dolly along the glass, reflections. Sound: air conditioning hum, silence.
shots.narration: Decades later, they were traced to Ahmedabad, in Gujarat. To a private museum collection. Together, they were valued at more than a hundred crore rupees.

shots.prompt: An elderly Tamil historian with grey hair and glasses at a cluttered wooden desk at night, comparing old black-and-white photographs of a bronze statue with a magnifying glass, piles of notebooks and palm-leaf manuscripts, a desk lamp. Slow push-in. Sound: pages turning, clock ticking.
shots.narration: It took years of work by historians who kept the old photographs and records. And a court order to reopen the case.

shots.prompt: Tamil Nadu police officers in khaki uniforms in a busy office, one officer spreads photographs of two bronze statues across a table covered with case files, others lean in. Tense, focused, daylight through window blinds. Sound: phones ringing, low voices.
shots.narration: In March 2018, the Tamil Nadu Idol Wing police registered a case. Within about ninety days, the bronzes were recovered.

shots.prompt: Daytime celebration on a street in Thanjavur: a joyful crowd showers flower petals on a decorated flower-covered palanquin carrying two antique bronze statues, nadaswaram players and drummers lead the procession, people with folded hands, some wiping tears. Modern Indian clothing. Slow tracking shot. Sound: nadaswaram, drums, cheering.
shots.narration: At the end of May 2018, Rajaraja and Lokamadevi returned to Tamil Nadu, and were taken home to Thanjavur. People lined the streets. Some of them wept.

shots.prompt: Slow cinematic push-in toward the temple tower at sunset, the sky glowing orange and red, birds flying across, silhouettes of people walking in the courtyard. Keep the architecture exactly as in the image. Sound: evening bells, birds, wind.
shots.narration: A thousand years after he built one of the greatest temples on earth, the king is back where he began. And yet, reports say the other bronzes from that same gift are still missing. Somewhere out there, the rest of this story is waiting.
